runs.name: Casella Waste Systems, Inc.; Nasdaq CWST, SEC CIK 0000911177; Rutland, Vermont, a regional, vertically integrated solid waste company in eleven states from Vermont to West Virginia, run as the Eastern, Western and Mid-Atlantic regions and Resource Solutions; Class B at ten votes a share; NCES landfill final day moved to 2026-12-31 by an 8-K of 2026-10-01; Ontario County Landfill to close at the end of 2028 by its host's vote; rivals named in the 10-K that file: Waste Management, Republic Services, Waste Connections
runs.box: OUT AT Q2 (the high-cost operator against the three rivals its 10-K names, the deciding part's disposal castle filling in; computation only beneath the stop)
runs.entry: The v5 re-run order, unattended work-hours cycle, one dispatched analyst under the canonical brief, from scratch. The brief's departures: the repository path after the move of 2026-10-25; the lines of evidence and competitors derived by the analyst from the 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7. Price **$89.39** (2026-10-29, live quote printed by tools/run.py, aggregator, flagged) x **63,640,046 shares** (Class A 62,651,846 and Class B 988,200, 10-Q cover as of 2026-07-15, accession 0000911177-26-000049; classes added, Class B convertible share for share with the same economics) = cap **$5,689M**; sovereign **5.37%** (US Treasury 30-year par, 2026-10-28). Filings: 10-K FY2025 0000911177-26-000008, the 10-Q above, DEF 14A 0001193125-26-161565, 8-Ks of 2026 including 0000911177-26-000052; operating cash FY2025 $329.8M cross-checked against the filed statement. **Q1 IN**: collection, transfer, landfill and recycling, the key variables filed yearly and slow-moving. **Q2 OUT**: the Western region decides, $449.0M of five-year segment operating income, 58% of the positive parts and more than the company's whole $390.0M; the Ontario County Landfill, permitted for 0.9M tons a year and the largest Western site, to close at the end of 2028 after its county board's vote of 2024-12-05; NCES takes its last waste on 2026-12-31 and the Dalton replacement, denied by New Hampshire on 2025-04-03, is called unlikely to run by the end of 2027; the 10-K concedes national rivals may have greater economies of scale; operating margin over the span Casella -2.4% to 8.8% (2012 to 2025, FY2025 3.5%) against Waste Management 7.7% to 18.7%, Republic 11.6% to 17.4%, Waste Connections 7.6% to 18.1% (2016 to 2025), Casella below each in every year but Waste Connections' 2020; pricing for the castle written down, price up 3.9% to 7.5% a year 2021 to 2025, not outweighing the cost gap; landfill capacity 107.2M to 98.2M tons 2023 to 2025. Q3 to Q12 NOT REACHED. Balance sheet: equity negative 2016 to 2018, rebuilt almost wholly by about $1.24B from four share offerings (2019 at $29.50, 2020 at $56.00, 2023 at $85.50, 2024 at $100.00), no buybacks; goodwill and intangibles $128M to $1,714M at 2026-06-30, tangible equity about -$134M; debt $509M (2016) to $1,351M; acquisition expense about $24M a year recurring. Facts after the stop, recorded not judged: a New Hampshire consent decree of 2026-01-12 with a $1.9M penalty over leachate management and leachate data and reporting at NCES; a $6.15M wage-and-hour class settlement in 2023; the Mid-Atlantic region losing money every year since bought. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash FY2021 to FY2025 after stock pay, all capital spending, finance-lease principal and tax at 21% federal (a CONVENTION of the run), all-equity mean $82.3M, equity-only $50.6M; $1,793M paid for businesses over the window and $400.8M in the first half of 2026, a serial acquirer on the organic pair, organic growth 6.7%; net debt $1,325.2M; value range all-equity, central, **$3.25 to $20.33 a share**, equity-only $14.82 to $25.33; fair price all-equity -$4.10, not positive, equity-only $10.29; about 2.1% and 1.2% at the price, no case earns the floor. Could not get: the rivals' segment margins, a maintenance and growth split of capital spending, earnings of the 2026 acquisitions, a state tax rate, Ontario County's share of revenue, the third-quarter 2026 10-Q. Framework gaps for the operator: Q2's ordinary-returns item written for a field of weak players and not one weak player in a strong field; the parts share above 100% under unallocated corporate costs; whether a service sold on bid is a commodity field; fuel surcharges as organic growth; whether the company's own tax includes state tax. Alternative box declared, TOO HARD (NATURE) on permit politics, not adopted, the deciding facts filed and not forecast. Write-early kept, five commits. Dispatcher's check: check_framework PASS; no E-ids, all 34 ids in the ledger, 12 adjacent fragment pairs checked by `dispatcher_check.py`, none flagged; the analyst's checker's four flags resolved by hand, three filing quotes and one paragraph-split mispairing (M2001-013, in its row); no citation slip; no tracked research file over 200 KB. Contamination declared: AQMS commit subjects, the dispatcher's lock file, the memory index, one file-name search of Test Runs for the name before the copy that returned nothing; none used. Position note filled at the fold: not held. Not armed: the box is not OUT at Q7 or IN.
runs.narr: OUT at Q2: the high-cost operator in a field whose three named rivals earn about twice its margin in every year, with the deciding Western region's largest landfill to close in 2028 by its host's vote and the Eastern NCES site ending 2026 with its replacement unlikely in time; equity rebuilt by four share offerings, tangible equity negative; a New Hampshire leachate consent decree recorded, not judged; computation only, all-equity value range $3.25 to $20.33 against $89.39. Not armed.
